explanation: This executable derives a rigid-package grasp and bowl placement from the runtime instruction, current RGB-D, calibration, and measured robot geometry; it contains no recorded waypoints or object poses. It separates a local differential motion witness from a transported envelope. A newly identified patch can support a prospective retention experiment without registration to the original corners. Only placement needs an envelope, obtained from a reliable saved patch-to-shape relation or a current plane/corner/two-edge model. The method uses bounded pose leases, independent object-versus-hand motion checks, bounded observation and registration recovery, and a low release followed by actual containment and stability observations. Numerical uncertainty allowances are heuristic, not calibrated confidence or collision certificates. All helper names, return fields, review schemas, and API arguments were audited against the supplied manual. This submission itself is not evidence of physical execution or official success.
interface:
Entry: main(api), with only the supplied globals and API. Returns a JSON-compatible object containing completion_proposed and evidence. evidence includes phase, exact unresolved gap, bounded diagnostics, measured retention, final observations, and remaining budgets. Runtime review interprets the requested item/container and accepts the observed rigid-box/open-bowl model; unsupported tasks are reported, not assigned invented geometry.

Observation dependency and gate interface:
1. Initial model. Required: same-body identity, visible planar top rectangle, stationary table support, inner bowl opening and an interior support point. Witnesses: two tight named RGB-D regions, eight distributed inner-lip points, floor, mark, and four visible top-vertex pixels. geo.plane uses coefficients; calibrated api.plane_point handles boundary depth contamination without inventing hidden vertices. Circle coverage/residuals, plane spreads, rectangle closure, orthogonality, normals, and positive thickness are checked numerically. Bottom extent is explicitly a box-on-measured-table model, not a measured hidden underside. Missing returned measurements are never indexed. Two distinct sample/view attempts are allowed; valid plane/opening components can be reused only at the identical physical frame. Physical dimensions remain a rigid-body invariant after manipulation, not a stationary world pose.

2. Open-finger approach. Required: projected width along the opposing tool-Y opening axis, pad offset/contact-band height, finger lower envelope, top/table heights, and current robot pose. Witnesses are the measured rectangle and proprioceptive geometry. The conservative open-gap proxy is twice joint separation minus the full pad Y span; it is not proof of contact. Candidate orientations preserve orientation first, then minimally yaw-align the short edge if needed. Three positive contact-overlap bands are considered, intersected with support-clearance constraints. Both nominal and uncertainty-limited margins are logged. A nominally supported small trial can be used when a conservative margin fails; subsequent measured retention, not pose attainment, decides its effect. An observed pregrasp body displacement invalidates the stationary grasp model. No useful nominal candidate yields a specific limitation, not a claim of physical impossibility.

3. Every local motion lease. Required: current pad/TCP distinction, requested orientation, immediate segment, relevant local load bound, and local external-obstruction evidence. Review receives calibrated projected action pixels, not purported object detections. Fields are obstruction={external,none_visible,unknown}, visibility={observed,partial,self_occluded,unobserved}, local={supported,unsupported,unknown}, change={consistent,item_moved,container_moved,unknown}, view_up={yes,no,unknown}. none_visible never means certified clearance; self-occlusion is not an external obstacle. A supported partially visible segment can proceed using the short-horizon model. Normal segments are at most 0.08 m; an unobserved segment uses at most 0.04 m only with explicit local support. Otherwise an independently justified 0.02 m upward observation action is possible once; an externally blocked direction can instead receive up to three independently reviewed upward alternatives. The rejected obstructed direction is not executed. There are 24 finite leg attempts, at most 16 Jev updates per lease, progress checks, and reserved verification resources. An unknown body observation alone does not assert motion. Table/bowl world priors survive only absent relevant contact or contradictory partial observations; an observed displacement invalidates them and stops that route. Grasp contact invalidates the old stationary item pose, not its measured dimensions.

4. Closure and prospective local reference. Required: a currently observable, physically defined item feature or usable textured patch before closure. Reference records retain identity, semantic feature definition, original point receipt, camera/polygon, frame, and tracker creation provenance. Same-body identity is separate from correspondence to a named feature. Two bounded close deliveries are acknowledged at the measured pose; neither delivery nor qpos proves grasp. The checkpoint records possible holding and jaw transitions before later sensing can fail. Repairs never reopen a possibly held item as initialization.

5. Retention. Required: independently observed corresponding local item positions before/after a small upward experiment, actual full robot states, and their relevant uncertainty. No perimeter or full-envelope registration is required. A tracker needs the correct reference_frame_id, at least 12 inliers, fraction at least 0.55, and spread relative to fit uncertainty. Unknown/poor tracking requests the exact saved physical feature in either view, with separate body and correspondence fields. Ambiguous correspondence is rejected. If neither old witness works, a newly identified patch and feature initialize a NEW gauge before another bounded experiment; this does not require old-corner registration. geo.attachment_error compares measured item motion against actual TCP motion. A 0.03 m intended lift must produce at least 0.015 m actual hand motion, independently measured upward item motion, and small discrepancy relative to that motion. Current residual noise and a shared reference term are kept distinct; shared error is propagated through actual orientation change rather than repeatedly charged as independent error. Clear static/lost-item evidence stops. Inconclusive evidence gets bounded new-reference trials, at most four physical tests in the episode. Pending test measurements survive repair.

6. Current transported envelope, only when needed. A good tracker transforms the previously measured shape and propagates lever-arm uncertainty. A landmark alone is deliberately NOT promoted to a complete transform. Executable fallback uses a current top-plane region, any visible physical top vertex, and points along its two inward incident edges, with retained dimensions. It does not demand original corner indices or visibility of all corners. Long/short ambiguity retains both geometrically supported assignments; overlong observed edge segments reject contradicted assignments, never assignments that merely give inconvenient margins. All remaining hypothesis vertices are propagated to placement. If no current model is obtainable after two distinct-view attempts, the method holds position and reports the envelope gap.

7. Transfer and opening fit. Required: relevant current XY envelope, bottom height for elevation, measured bowl center/radius/rim height, and current finger envelope; unrelated full-pose certainty is not required for a local retention test. Mean and bounding-box-center candidates are scored by their actual worst supported XY radius. Ordinary control tolerance is derived from placement slack, bounded by the documented 0.0005-0.003 m range. Transfer compares fresh independent local motion with actual hand motion after each lease. Unknown registration or an inconsistent effect triggers a new bounded retention experiment without opening. Opening uncertainty can be reduced by new inner-rim samples. Positive nominal but inconclusive conservative fit can authorize a labeled low-release trial, not a clearance assertion. Current geometry is remeasured after centering and lowering; planned control error is not charged again as an unobserved displacement. The release height keeps both inferred object bottom and measured finger envelope above the rim. An actually nonpositive current opening fit forbids release.

8. Release and final goal. Required: actual item/bowl relation, visible resting support, and independent short-horizon stability. After acknowledged opening, the hand withdraws to produce a new view. Up to three structured reviews measure a persistent physical feature and classify relation={inside_bowl,outside_bowl,unknown}, support={settled_on_interior,falling_or_sliding,unknown}, correspondence={same,new,unknown}. Two corresponding world measurements at different physical frames, separated by acknowledged control steps, must agree within 0.003 m and both support containment, with current visible resting support. A missing sample does not erase a useful prior one. A bounded lateral empty-hand view is available for an unresolved final observation. No post-release unknown authorizes regrasping. Positive completion is only a proposal, never native evaluator success.

Persistence/bounds: one method checkpoint contains fixed-size geometry, one active reference/handle, one pending test, one same-frame observation cache, jaw acknowledgments, phase intent, and eight diagnostics capped at 512 characters each. Clouds and tracker inlier histories are not checkpointed; shape sets contain at most 16 vertices. No nested historical checkpoint copies are made. Cache is discarded on entry after repair, but references/handles and acknowledged physical phase persist; a fresh track_update is required before using restored registration. Same-frame cache reuse within one execution does not advance physics or replace a changed-frame observation. The worst fixed structures fit the checkpoint limits. All observation helpers return inconclusive locally into the caller's actual alternative or a precise bounded terminal limitation. Programming/API errors are not silently treated as successful sensing.
jev_protocol:
All physical commands use api.control, directly for jaw/stability updates or through api.drive for ordinary bounded pose-feedback leases. Seven self-contained choice questions are supplied on every call. For each x,y,z,rx,ry,rz question, the subject and state.processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation selector are explicit: decrease -> negative, within_tolerance -> hold, increase -> positive. Translation signs are world-coordinate signs; rotation signs are world rotation-vector signs. Quaternions are xyzw, and api.compose supplies justified world-yaw changes. Gripper choices are exactly open/close/keep, selected from state.processed_features.objective.gripper; keep never means open.

Program features sent to control are phase, local review classifications and numerical tolerance, or jaw-transition/stability intent. The host supplies trusted robot state, actual residuals, axis relations, objective, controller limits, and source labels. Jev is not asked to calculate metrics, infer image measurements, run Python, or decide task success. The host maps Jev's unchanged axis choices to the documented signed bounded magnitudes/deadbands. The program checks actual receipts and state afterward; it does not replace an inconvenient Jev answer.

Pose control uses pad_center, explicitly accounting for the rotated TCP-to-pad offset and measured finger geometry. Translation limits are 0.001-0.02 m, rotation limits 0.01-0.08 rad, and updates use three native steps. drive status reached is only a robot/gripper-delivery fact. lease_exhausted/moved permit only bounded progress with a new local assessment; stalled or negligible progress stops rather than repeatedly pushing contact. Whole-lease effect tests save api.state before and after; receipt before/after are correctly treated as TCP position lists, not full states.

api.review, not Jev text choices, requests current image evidence with exact typed fields and named supported points/regions. Every call supplies fields, including all recovery/final branches. Pixels and polygons are numeric arrays with explicit lengths; unavailable geometry uses null and categorical unknown/ambiguous values. Selected pixels are not assumed measured: membership and measurement_errors are checked first. Structured schema validity never certifies visual truth. Numeric fits, widths, clearances, transformed envelopes, uncertainty allowances, attachment discrepancies, progress, and final drift are computed in code. False, unknown, and positive measured outcomes lead to different executable branches. No hidden task predicates, force sensing, segmentation IDs, simulator state, or collision planner are requested.
